newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka plans lottery to raise money for disable.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka plans lottery to raise money for disable.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Thursday proposed a weekly lottery to raise money for rehabilitating the country's disabled.

Media Minister Managla Samaraweera told a news conference in Colombo that there were some 720,000 disabled people in the country, but the government did not have enough money for their welfare and rehabilitation.

"According to the World Health Organisation, four percent of Sri Lanka's population is disabled. Funds available in the social services sector for their welfare and rehabilitation are 54 million rupees ($920,000) each year," the minister said.
"Therefore, it was decided to raise extra funds, and a lottery was found to be a way to do it," he said.
Sri Lanka is fighting a 13-year-old ethnic war against Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels, who demand a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian ocean island's north and east.
Hundreds of people lose limbs each year on the battlefield or as a result of mines in civilian areas in the north and east, officials say.
